Just an overview. For example, when can you or can't you charge for software? Do you have to provide source code? Etc.

Probably should go in /v/opensource but that place is dead.
Can someone please explain the GPL? The good and bad?

You must provide the changes you make to the source. You may charge for the software, but you have to provide the source for free. You may also sell GPL software together with proprietary software, like most Andriod phones.

Other licences lice BSD and MIT licences don't need the release of changed source code. Some open source people which ones make the software more free.

my fren, you do not have to provide the "changes", you have to provide the source code, but you can charge money for the source code and allow the users the freedom to modify, add, subtract, and resell their changes, and their source under the GPL too.

http://choosealicense.com/licenses/gpl-3.0/

In general I've found that choosealicense.com/ has been useful.

You can always charge for software.

GPL means the source code is the product. If you charge for your product, you have to provide the source at no extra charge.

GPL code can be shared and modified and the modification re-sold, but remains GPL.

In practice it matters little. Most people don't care about the source code. It is good to have it in any case.
